result.evidence_A: About 113 words, coherent. Covers problem, method, and the 48%/6% finding accurately. Defect: 'less accurate than the target' misstates the validity condition, which is smaller fidelity. Says 'two representative error processes', though the body only clearly shows random-channel results. 'Consistently reduce' matches 'always results in more accurate approximations'.
result.evidence_B: About 150 words, slightly over the ~147 limit. Informal tone ('You lose a lot', 'You will still need'). Claims 'four new' channels, but PC is the existing baseline. Vague fidelity constraint. Implies the diamond norm is required rather than more natural. Omits the PC/CC/PMC/CMC ordering and claims of overall improvement.
result.comparative_reason: Both state the 48% result. A is concise and within length, uses abstract style, and has one validity misstatement. B has more defects: it exceeds the length limit, uses an informal register, wrongly counts four new channels, and overstates the diamond-norm requirement.
